origin.note: Runs on the v2 fixture, where passcodes shipped and still ask the owner: the defect walk 25's live check caught.

title: A passcode switch beside access, with a Passcode mark, and members never asked
objective: Passcodes can already be set per link. Make them visible and fix who is asked. On the library list, a row whose document has any passcode-protected link shows a "Passcode" mark (data-testid="mark-passcode"); on the document page, a protected link row reads "Passcode" too. The people in the document's library are never asked for a passcode: signed in (userId on GET /l/:linkId, or linkPage(store, linkId, { userId })) they open a protected link directly, and their open is counted as theirs. Anyone else is still asked.
acceptance: A row whose document has a protected link shows the Passcode mark; others do not
The protected link row on the document page reads Passcode
A signed-in library member opens a protected link without being asked, on the API and the page
A signed-in non-member and a visitor are still asked
plan_summary: Read hasPasscode in the pages; let a member through the visitor gate in api.mjs and linkPage.
